newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chnernomyrdin, Chechen leader discuss oil pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Chnernomyrdin, Chechen leader discuss oil pipeline.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin met the president of Chechnya on Thursday for talks partially devoted to the breakaway region's oil pipeline.
"I think tomorrow there will be some results from these talks," Chechen leader Aslan Maskhadov told reporters in remarks broadcast on Russian Public Television.
Chernomyrdin said they would resume discussions on Friday in the Black Sea resort of Sochi, where he is on vacation. He said he had discussed mostly economic problems with Maskhadov.
Maskhadov's remarks appeared to hint that an agreement might be signed on Friday, but he gave no details.
Russian Fuel and Oil Minister Boris Nemtsov said last month Russia was confident of raising the $2 million needed by Chechnya to finish repairing a damaged oil pipeline on its territory.
The Chechen section of the pipeline runs from the Caspian Sea to Russian export outlets in the Black Sea.

Among attending Thursday's talks included the secretary of the Russian Security Council Ivan Rybkin, the president of the Southern Oil Company or YUNKO and the head of the Chechen national bank, Itar-Tass news agency reported.
Russian President Boris Yeltsin and Maskhadov signed a peace accord last month promising to end 400 years of intermittent conflict between Moscow and the independence-minded north Caucasus region.
Moscow last sent in troops in December 1994, launching a 21-month war which failed to crush Chechnya's independence moves.
